- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 5–10% for the immediate follow-up days.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), check sentiment for bullish bias — if present, consider mean reversion in next 7–10 days.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome (e.g., >10% under for 3+ days), sentiment may be bearish — consider upward adjustment if sentiment turns positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags true trend by 1–3 days; align forecast with sentiment momentum rather than historical mean.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often fails to catch the momentum — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — if last 3–5 days show strong sentiment reversal, don’t extrapolate trend; use sentiment to guide correction instead.
